## Proof

**Setup.** Six islands with every pair connected gives the complete graph $K_6$, which has $\binom{6}{2}=15$ edges. Choosing a set of inactive cables is the same as choosing a set of active cables (its complement). The bureau requires the active cables to keep all six islands connected, so we must count the number of **connected spanning subgraphs** of $K_6$, i.e., the number of connected labeled graphs on 6 vertices.

**Notation.** Let $g(n)=2^{\binom{n}{2}}$ be the total number of labeled graphs on $n$ vertices, and $c(n)$ the number of **connected** labeled graphs on $n$ vertices.

**Recurrence.** Fix a distinguished vertex (say vertex 1). In any labeled graph on $n$ vertices, let the connected component containing vertex 1 have exactly $k$ vertices ($1\le k\le n$). We choose the other $k-1$ members of this component from the remaining $n-1$ vertices in $\binom{n-1}{k-1}$ ways; this component must be connected ($c(k)$ ways); the remaining $n-k$ vertices form an arbitrary graph ($g(n-k)$ ways). Hence

$$g(n)=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\binom{n-1}{k-1}\,c(k)\,g(n-k),\qquad c(n)=g(n)-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\binom{n-1}{k-1}\,c(k)\,g(n-k).$$

**Base case.** $g(1)=1,\;c(1)=1$.

**Compute up to $n=6$.**

| $n$ | $g(n)=2^{\binom n2}$ | $c(n)$ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | $1$ | $1$ |
| 2 | $2$ | $2-1=1$ |
| 3 | $8$ | $8-2-2=4$ |
| 4 | $64$ | $64-8-6-12=38$ |
| 5 | $1024$ | $1024-64-32-48-152=728$ |
| 6 | $32768$ | see below |

**Detailed computation for $n=6$.**

$$c(6)=32768-\sum_{k=1}^{5}\binom{5}{k-1}c(k)\,g(6-k).$$

| $k$ | $\binom{5}{k-1}$ | $c(k)$ | $g(6-k)$ | product |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 | $g(5)=1024$ | $1024$ |
| 2 | 5 | 1 | $g(4)=64$ | $320$ |
| 3 | 10 | 4 | $g(3)=8$ | $320$ |
| 4 | 10 | 38 | $g(2)=2$ | $760$ |
| 5 | 5 | 728 | $g(1)=1$ | $3640$ |

Sum of subtracted terms: $1024+320+320+760+3640=6064$.

$$c(6)=32768-6064=26704.$$

**Interpretation.** Each connected labeled graph on 6 vertices corresponds to exactly one valid choice of active cables, hence exactly one valid set of inactive cables (its complement). Therefore the number of different sets of inactive cables the bureau can choose is

$$\boxed{26704}.$$
